title: TagDuel action transaction rollback under SQLite write faults
scenarios: A SQLite trigger aborts INSERT into tag_transition_events after actTag has computed and attempted to persist the new session. The transaction must restore the exact tag_sessions row, event list, action receipts, four locks, player rows, and collection rows; after dropping the trigger, the same request_id and revision must commit exactly once.

A SQLite trigger aborts INSERT into tag_action_receipts after the session update and transition event write. The transaction must roll back all three writes together; retrying the identical request must commit one event and one receipt, and replay must not advance the revision or duplicate events.
invariants: Session revision, status, updated timestamp, members and serialized duel state are atomic with transition events and action receipts.
Failed writes do not consume or duplicate physical card UIDs.
All four participant locks remain intact when a duel action transaction fails.
Player rows and player_cards remain unchanged by TagDuel action rollback.
The exact same request_id can be retried after a failed transaction because no receipt was committed.
Successful replay is idempotent and does not append a second transition event.
limits: Tests use a temporary SQLite database and real compiled TagStore/TagDuel modules.
The tests inject SQLite write failures; they do not simulate process termination or power loss.
No runtime, resolver, catalog manifest, allowlist, persistent database or player data is modified.
This is a TagDuel storage-integrity regression and certifies no new card behavior.
No live Discord API session is performed.
command: npm run check && npm run build && node --test tests/tagActionRollbackAtomicity2v2.test.cjs
